examples.en: I looked across through the window at the house opposite.

examples.ko: 강 건너편 마을을 건너다보니 불빛이 반짝여요.
examples.en: Looking across at the village on the other side of the river, lights sparkle.

examples.ko: 친구가 길 건너에서 이쪽을 건너다보고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is looking this way from across the road.

examples.ko: 아이가 창가에 서서 강 건너편 산을 건너다봐요.
examples.en: The child stands by the window and looks across the river at the mountain.

examples.ko: 건너다보면 바다 쪽에 작은 섬이 보여요.
examples.en: If you look across, you can see a small island near the sea.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말없이 저를 건너다보기만 했어요.
examples.en: He just looked across at me without saying a word.

explain: 멀리 떨어진 맞은편을 바라볼 때 써요. 위쪽을 향해 보는 '쳐다보다'와 달라요. 담이나 울타리 너머로 보는 건 '넘겨다보다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child is looking across the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 맞은편을 보고 있는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of looking across right now.

phrases.en: I can see the sea across from the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞은편이 눈에 보일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the far side is visible.

phrases.en: I looked across at the house opposite.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at the opposite side

explain_en: You use it when looking at something far away on the opposite side. It is different from '쳐다보다', which means looking up at something. Looking over a wall or fence is '넘겨다보다'.

examples.en: I walked through every alley of Seoul taking photos.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 골목골목마다 작은 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has a small shop in every alley.
The delivery driver knows every alley.
A delicious smell comes from every alley.
I want to wander around every nook and alley.

examples.ko: 골목골목 불이 켜지니 동네가 아늑해 보여요.
examples.en: With the lights on in every alley, the neighborhood looks cozy.

explain: '골목'을 겹쳐서 이 골목 저 골목 전부라는 느낌을 줘요. '마다'나 '을/에서'와 자주 쓰고, '곳곳', '구석구석'과 비슷한 느낌으로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: There are pretty cafes in every alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마다'를 붙이면 빠짐없이 모든 골목이라는 뜻이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '마다' strengthens the sense of 'every single alley'.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 시장 골목골목을 누비며 구경했어요.
phrases.en: I wandered through every alley of the market all day.
There are parks all over the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골목골목'보다 범위가 넓어서 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It covers a wider range than '골목골목' and fits any place.

explain_en: Doubling '골목' gives the feel of this alley, that alley, all of them. It is often used with '마다', '을' or '에서', and feels similar to '곳곳' or '구석구석'.

examples.en: A monument stands in the middle of the square.
I took photos with friends in front of the monument.

examples.ko: 이 기념탑은 오래전 일을 기억하려고 세웠어요.
examples.en: This monument was built to remember something from long ago.
There's also a small monument at the entrance of the village.
I went early in the morning to see the monument.
The area around the monument is neatly kept.

explain: 어떤 일이나 사람을 기억하려고 탑 모양으로 높이 세운 것을 말해요. 비슷한 '기념비'는 비석 모양이라서 모양이 달라요. '기념탑을 세우다, 기념탑이 서 있다'처럼 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 기억하려고 새로 만들 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase for building one to remember something.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 잘 띄어서 약속 장소로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easy to spot, so it is often used as a meeting place.

phrases.en: I went to see the monument on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하러 가는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the purpose of going to see it.

explain_en: It is a tall structure shaped like a tower, built to remember an event or person. The similar '기념비' is a stone-tablet type, so the shape differs. You say '기념탑을 세우다' or '기념탑이 서 있다'.

examples.ko: 마당 수돗가에서 아이들이 손을 씻고 있어요.
examples.en: The kids are washing their hands at the outdoor tap in the yard.

examples.ko: 시골집 수돗가에서 빨래를 했던 기억이 나요.
examples.en: I remember doing laundry at the tap of our country house.
The tap area on the playground is crowded every lunch break.
Water has spilled around the tap, so the floor is slippery.
After coming down from the hike, I washed my shoes at the tap.
There is a small flower bed next to the tap.

explain: 집 마당, 학교 운동장, 공원처럼 야외에 수도꼭지가 있는 곳을 말해서, 실내의 '싱크대'나 '세면대'와는 달라요. 사이시옷이 들어가서 '수돗가'라고 써요.

phrases.en: I washed my shoes at the outdoor tap.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for washing with water outdoors.

phrases.en: There is a small flower bed next to the outdoor tap.
I drank water at the tap on the playground.
phrases.nuance_en: Names a place commonly seen at schools.

explain_en: It refers to the spot with a tap outdoors, such as a yard, a school playground or a park, unlike an indoor '싱크대' (sink) or '세면대' (washbasin). It is written with a sai-siot, as '수돗가'.

examples.en: A patrol car is parked in front of the police substation.
A patrol car goes around our neighborhood every night.

examples.ko: 순찰차를 보면 운전을 더 조심하게 돼요.
examples.en: When I see a patrol car, I drive more carefully.

examples.ko: 순찰차 한 대가 사이렌을 켜고 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A patrol car passed by with its siren on.
The police officer got out of the patrol car and asked me for directions.

examples.ko: 아파트 입구에 순찰차가 있어서 마음이 놓여요.
examples.en: There is a patrol car at the apartment entrance, so I feel safe.

explain: 일상에서는 '경찰차'라고도 많이 말해요. 순찰차는 동네를 돌며 살피는 차라는 느낌이 있어서 '순찰차가 돌다', '순찰차를 보다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: A police car is at the scene of the accident.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life people also say 경찰차 a lot.

phrases.en: A patrol car goes around the alley every evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동네를 돌며 살피는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a car going around and watching over a neighborhood.
phrases.en_equiv: a patrol car makes its rounds

phrases.en: I feel safe when I see a patrol car on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 마주친 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for seeing one on the road.

explain_en: In daily talk people also say '경찰차' (police car). 순찰차 carries the feel of a car that goes around an area keeping watch, so phrases like '순찰차가 돌다' (a patrol car makes its rounds) are common.
